title: Outcome Monitors: Recovery Affordances for Silent Tool Failures
authors: Sugam Panthi; Rabab Abdelfattah
central_claim: Post-execution contract checks on tool results with nonbinding receipts naming recovery tools raise ToolMaze completion 10.9% to 28.1%; the monitor never repairs; out-of-vocabulary detection ~46%.
cite_claim: Closest prior runtime monitor: checks returned results against mined outcome contracts, preserves the raw result, and leaves recovery to the agent; it never executes a repair. Existing claim C11.
location: Abstract; Sec. 3 (Alg. 1); Table 2; Appendix G Table 9
quote: it never restricts an action, executes a repair, reveals a benchmark fault label, or consults the evaluator
relevance: Direct competitor for Observe step; defines the detection-only baseline; reuse C11.

title: When Tools Fail: Benchmarking Dynamic Replanning and Anomaly Recovery in LLM Agents
authors: Dongsheng Zhu; Xuchen Ma; Yucheng Shen; Xiang Li; Yukun Zhao; Shuaiqiang Wang; Lingyong Yan; Dawei Yin
central_claim: ToolMaze benchmark: implicit semantic tool failures cause the sharpest drop in recovery (~37% PRR) because agents trust corrupted outputs.
cite_claim: Implicit semantic tool failures degrade agent recovery most; agents over-trust corrupted outputs.
quote: complex topologies trap agents in futile trial-and-error loops
relevance: Motivates silent-fault focus; benchmark used by Outcome Monitors; candidate external benchmark.

title: ToolGate: Contract-Grounded and Verified Tool Execution for LLMs
authors: Yanming Liu; Xinyue Peng; Jiannan Cao; Xinyi Wang; Songhang Deng; Jintao Chen; Jianwei Yin; Xuhong Zhang
central_claim: Each tool gets a Hoare-style pre/postcondition; postconditions on structure, type, range and format decide whether a result may update a trusted state; failing results are discarded.
cite_claim: Postcondition checks on tool outputs exist in prior work, but a failing result is discarded and the next tool tried; nothing is persisted and the tool is not fixed.
quote: If verification fails, the result is discarded entirely, preventing contaminated outputs from propagating
relevance: Closest 'contract on tool output' gate; contrasts discard vs fiks receipt+repair.

title: verimcp: a trusted agent stack for MCP (PyPI package and repo)
authors: Rudra Naresh
central_claim: Transparent MCP proxy that, for calls it knows how to check, re-derives the real outcome (re-read file, git log, CI) and rewrites a false success into an error; also idempotent replay of verified calls.
cite_claim: An open-source MCP proxy already performs post-call outcome re-derivation (read-after-write style) for git/file/CI tools; it does not create tests or fix the server.
quote: independently re-derive the real outcome (re-read the file, re-check the git log, re-run the safe parts of a CI step)
relevance: Closest open-source MCP product to fiks's read-after-write postconditions; MIT; candidate baseline/design comparison for D3.

title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures
authors: Sunny Dubey
central_claim: Telemetry monitor (one-class ESN + CUSUM) plus deterministic recompute layer; flagged runs are rolled back and re-run, raising task success 52% to 73%.
cite_claim: 'Repair' in agent-monitoring work typically means re-running the agent, not changing tool code.
quote: each flagged run is rolled back and re-run live
relevance: Agent-side remedy baseline; contrast with tool-side repair.

title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
authors: Haoyu Wang; Christopher M. Poskitt; Jun Sun
central_claim: DSL of rules (trigger, predicates, enforcement) enforced at runtime; triggers before actions, on state change, or at finish; ms overhead; LLM-generated rules.
cite_claim: Runtime enforcement DSLs for agents check planned actions at discrete checkpoints and enforce by user inspection, self-examination, a predefined action, or stopping.
quote: Rules combine triggers, predicates, and enforcement mechanisms [verify exact wording against abstract]
relevance: Canonical pre-execution enforcement DSL; LangChain-only; weak fit as baseline but required related work.

title: Symbolic Temporal Supervision of LLM Agents Using Contracts (ContrAgent)
authors: Yifeng Xiao; Pierluigi Nuzzo
central_claim: LTLf assume/guarantee contracts compiled to DFAs; one deterministic artifact gates online and audits recorded traces offline; return events are checked; AgentDojo ASR 47.7% to 0.79%.
cite_claim: Formal contract monitors can both gate agent tool calls online and audit recorded traces offline with deterministic per-contract verdicts.
quote: no single deterministic artifact supports both roles
relevance: Strongest formal-RV competitor; Apache-2.0; offline replay CLI makes it a runnable baseline on fiks traces.

title: Agent Behavioral Contracts: Formal Specification and Runtime Enforcement for Reliable Autonomous AI Agents
authors: Varun Pratap Bhardwaj
central_claim: Design-by-Contract for agents: preconditions, hard/soft invariants, governance, recovery; 200-scenario benchmark across 7 models; <10 ms overhead.
cite_claim: Design-by-Contract has been applied to agents at the session/action level (preconditions, invariants, governance, recovery), not as postconditions on tool outputs.
quote: Reference implementation and benchmark suite available subject to intellectual property clearance.
relevance: DbC lineage for agents; not runnable (IP-gated, CC BY-NC-ND).

title: Formal Runtime Verification for Tool-Using LLM Agents: An Offline Same-Benchmark Study on AgentDojo and STAC
authors: Nikolaos Kekatos; Stylianos Basagiannis; Marinelio Chintri; Alexios Lekidis; Tom Nianios; Ioannis Seitoglou; Anastasios Temperekidis; Panagiotis Katsaros
central_claim: MFOTL obligations via MonPoly on recorded traces flag ~70-72% of attacks but fire on 29.3% of benign runs; temporal monitoring helps only when the trace exposes trustworthy history.
cite_claim: Classical RV tools (MonPoly/MFOTL) applied offline to agent traces show high benign firing for generic obligations and depend on trustworthy trace history.
quote: formal temporal monitoring adds value exactly when the trace exposes trustworthy history
relevance: Supports fiks recording the raw upstream exchange as trustworthy history; FP denominator caution.

title: VIGIL: Runtime Enforcement of Behavioral Specifications in AI Agent Skills
authors: Ying Li; Yanju Chen; Hongbo Wen; Bosi Zhang; Hanzhi Liu; Peiran Wang; Yu Feng; Yuan Tian
central_claim: Policies over agent-tool events (ordering, argument constraints, cross-call value flow) reduced to SMT over finite traces; >95% recall, <10% FPR.
cite_claim: Recent runtime enforcement targets temporal ordering and value flow across tool calls, i.e., safety/compliance policies.
quote: VIGIL detects policy violations with over 95% recall and a false-positive rate below 10%.
relevance: Pre-execution/temporal cluster; whether it inspects return values is unconfirmed.

title: AgentLTL: A Trace-Verification Framework for Measuring, Enforcing, and Training Procedural Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
authors: Laila Elkoussy; Julien Perez
central_claim: FO-LTL rules over agent traces give a deterministic compliance score usable for auditing, blocking tool calls, and as a training reward.
cite_claim: Temporal-logic trace checkers for agents target procedural compliance and can double as rewards.
quote: In safety-critical settings, the procedure itself is part of correctness.
relevance: Related work for temporal/procedural monitors.

title: Reason Less, Verify More: Deterministic Gates Recover a Silent Policy-Violation Failure Mode in Tool-Using LLM Agents
authors: Vikas Reddy; Sumanth Reddy Challaram; Abhishek Basu
central_claim: Four read-only checks before each write block policy-violating writes; tau2-airline success 29.6% to 42.0% on gpt-4o-mini. Existing claim C8.
cite_claim: Deterministic pre-write gates prevent a known class of silent policy-violating writes but do not guarantee task success.
quote: can deterministically prevent a known class of silent policy-violating writes
relevance: Reuse C8; pre-execution counterpart to fiks's post-execution read-after-write.

title: ProbGuard: Proactive Runtime Monitoring for LLM Agent Safety via Probabilistic Prediction
authors: Haoyu Wang; Christopher M. Poskitt; Jiali Wei; Jun Sun
central_claim: Learns a DTMC over symbolic states from traces and intervenes when predicted probability of staying safe drops below a threshold.
cite_claim: Probabilistic runtime monitors predict safety violations ahead of time from learned trace models.
quote: ProbGuard consistently predicts traffic law violations and collisions in advance
relevance: Related work (safety, predictive); not about tool output correctness.

title: VeriGuard: Enhancing LLM Agent Safety via Verified Code Generation
authors: Lesly Miculicich; Mihir Parmar; Hamid Palangi; Krishnamurthy Dj Dvijotham; Mirko Montanari; Tomas Pfister; Long T. Le
venue_or_publisher: arXiv 2510.05156 (Google; ACL 2026 per Google Research listing [verify])
central_claim: Policy code is verified offline (tests + formal verification) and then used at runtime to check each proposed action before execution.
cite_claim: Verified policy monitors check proposed agent actions before execution.
quote: to validate each proposed agent action against the pre-verified policy before execution.
relevance: Pre-execution cluster; verification applies to the policy, not to tools.

title: ToolSafe: Enhancing Tool Invocation Safety of LLM-based agents via Proactive Step-level Guardrail and Feedback
authors: Yutao Mou; Zhangchi Xue; Lijun Li; Peiyang Liu; Shikun Zhang; Wei Ye; Jing Shao
venue_or_publisher: arXiv 2601.10156 (Findings of ACL 2026 per ACL Anthology listing [verify])
central_claim: RL-trained guard model detects unsafe tool invocations before execution; feedback framework cuts harmful invocations ~65%.
cite_claim: Learned step-level guardrails judge tool invocations before execution, for safety rather than functional correctness.
quote: The model proactively detects unsafe tool invocation actions before execution by reasoning over the interaction history.
relevance: Pre-execution learned guard; related work.

title: ShieldAgent: Shielding Agents via Verifiable Safety Policy Reasoning
authors: Zhaorun Chen; Mintong Kang; Bo Li
central_claim: Guard agent extracts verifiable rules from policy documents into probabilistic rule circuits and checks protected agents' action trajectories; 90.1% recall on ShieldAgent-Bench.
cite_claim: Guardrail agents verify action trajectories against safety policies, not the correctness of tool results.
quote: enforce explicit safety policy compliance for the action trajectory of other protected agents through logical reasoning
relevance: Safety-trajectory cluster; contrast in related work.

title: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
authors: Zhen Xiang; Linzhi Zheng; Yanjie Li; Junyuan Hong; Qinbin Li; Han Xie; Jiawei Zhang; Zidi Xiong; Chulin Xie; Carl Yang; Dawn Song; Bo Li
central_claim: LLM guard agent plans from guard requests and generates guardrail code to check target agent actions; >98% on EICU-AC, 83% on Mind2Web-SC.
cite_claim: LLM guard agents generate code to check whether another agent's actions satisfy guard requests.
quote: dynamically checking whether their actions satisfy given safety guard requests
relevance: Safety/access-control cluster; related work.

title: LlamaFirewall: An open source guardrail system for building secure AI agents
authors: Sahana Chennabasappa; Cyrus Nikolaidis; Daniel Song; David Molnar; et al.; Joshua Saxe
central_claim: Three scanners: PromptGuard 2 (jailbreak/injection in prompts and untrusted data such as tool outputs), AlignmentCheck (reasoning audit), CodeShield (static analysis); AgentDojo ASR 17.6% to 1.75%.
cite_claim: Production security guardrails scan tool outputs as untrusted input for injection, not for functional correctness.
quote: a fine-tuned BERT-style model that detects direct jailbreak attempts with high accuracy and low latency
relevance: Negative-control baseline (pip install llamafirewall); shows security vs functional split.

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
authors: Edoardo Debenedetti; Ilia Shumailov; Tianqi Fan; Jamie Hayes; Nicholas Carlini; Daniel Fabian; Christoph Kern; Chongyang Shi; Andreas Terzis; Florian Tramer
central_claim: Separates control and data flow so untrusted tool data cannot change program flow; capabilities enforce policies at tool-call time; 77% AgentDojo tasks with provable security.
cite_claim: System-level defenses treat tool outputs as untrusted data that must not steer control flow; they do not check whether the data is correct.
quote: the untrusted data retrieved by the LLM can never impact the program flow
relevance: Security cluster; related work.

title: NeMo Guardrails: A Toolkit for Controllable and Safe LLM Applications with Programmable Rails
authors: Traian Rebedea; Razvan Dinu; Makesh Sreedhar; Christopher Parisien; Jonathan Cohen
central_claim: Programmable rails written in Colang, runtime sits between user and LLM.
cite_claim: NeMo Guardrails adds programmable rails to LLM applications.
quote: NeMo Guardrails allows developers to add programmable rails to LLM applications
relevance: Industry guardrail framework; see nemo-tool-rails for tool-result scope.

title: NeMo Guardrails: Tool Calling rails (guardrail catalog) and Rail Types
authors: NVIDIA
central_claim: IORails tool-result rail checks linkage to prior call, id uniqueness, name consistency and content shape; fails closed; does not enforce a response schema or check content.
cite_claim: The main open-source guardrail framework's tool-result rail is structural only and explicitly does not enforce a declared response schema.
location: Tool Calling page, 'What it checks' / limitations; Rail Types page ('Execution rails')
quote: does not yet enforce a declared response schema
relevance: Runnable structural baseline (H-RM3).

title: Invariant Guardrails (invariantlabs-ai/invariant)
authors: Invariant Labs (now Snyk)
central_claim: Python-like rule language over messages, ToolCall and ToolOutput; Gateway evaluates rules on each LLM and MCP request before and after; Apache-2.0.
cite_claim: Rule-based guardrails can match on tool outputs and are deployed as a transparent LLM/MCP gateway; rules raise violations, they do not fix tools.
quote: automatically evaluates your rules on each LLM and MCP request (before and after)
relevance: Runnable baseline: same rules in a different engine + default security rules as negative control.

title: Snyk acquires Invariant Labs to expand AI agent security capabilities
authors: SiliconANGLE (news)
central_claim: Snyk acquired Invariant Labs (ETH Zurich spin-off) for its AI Trust Platform.
cite_claim: Invariant Labs' guardrails and MCP scanning became part of Snyk in June 2025 (security positioning).
quote: Snyk Ltd. today announced that it has acquired Invariant Labs AG, a Swiss artificial intelligence security research firm [verify exact wording]
relevance: Market context: MCP guardrails are sold as security.

title: Guardrails AI (guardrails-ai/guardrails)
authors: Guardrails AI
central_claim: Python framework whose Guards intercept LLM inputs and outputs and apply validators (Hub, Pydantic, RAIL); Apache-2.0.
cite_claim: Output-validation libraries validate LLM inputs/outputs with typed validators; they are not wired to tool results by default.
quote: intercept the inputs and outputs of LLMs
relevance: Runnable typed/range validator baseline (H-RM3).

title: MCP TypeScript SDK v2 docs: Tools (outputSchema / structuredContent)
authors: Model Context Protocol
central_claim: The SDK validates structuredContent against outputSchema before the result leaves the server and advertises the schema so clients can validate too.
cite_claim: Schema validation of tool results is built into the MCP SDK, so schema-only checking is the protocol-native baseline. Relates to C26.
quote: The SDK validates structuredContent against outputSchema before the result leaves your server.
relevance: Schema-only baseline arm.

title: From Confident Closing to Silent Failure: Characterizing False Success in LLM Agents
authors: Laksh Advani
central_claim: LLM judges do not exceed AUROC 0.65 at detecting false success on tau2-bench; lightweight classifiers reach 0.83. Existing claim C7.
cite_claim: LLM-as-judge monitors are weak at detecting outcomes that require environment state they cannot see.
quote: no configuration across 5 judges, 5 prompt strategies, and full task specifications exceeds AUROC 0.65 on tau2-bench
relevance: Reuse C7; motivates grounded checks and H-RM4.

title: AgentAuditor: Human-Level Safety and Security Evaluation for LLM Agents
authors: Hanjun Luo; Shenyu Dai; Chiming Ni; Xinfeng Li; Guibin Zhang; Kun Wang; Tongliang Liu; Hanan Salam
central_claim: Memory-augmented, training-free LLM judge reaches human-level accuracy on agent safety/security labeling (ASSEBench, R-Judge).
cite_claim: Strongest case for LLM-as-judge monitors: human-level accuracy on transcript-visible safety risks.
quote: training-free, memory-augmented reasoning framework that empowers LLM evaluators to emulate human expert evaluators
relevance: Strong counterpoint for H-RM4; note task difference (visible risk vs hidden state).

title: AgentCheck: A Reproduce-Intervene-Mitigate Workbench for LLM Agents over MCP
authors: Aritra Mazumder; Nusrat Jahan Lia
central_claim: Records an agent's real MCP tool responses, replays with 12 fault types, lets developers toggle a mitigation and re-check; most failures were silent confident use of bad output; stale-data faults resist retry.
cite_claim: Closest reproduce-and-mitigate loop over MCP; mitigations are agent-side (e.g., retry), not changes to the MCP server.
quote: AgentCheck runs an agent against its real tools and records every tool response
relevance: Nearest record/replay prior art; supports silent-failure framing; contrast on tool-side repair.

title: CatchBench: When Can an Agent Failure Be Caught?
authors: Yue Zhao; Mengyuan Li; Ruolin Li; Prince Zizhuang Wang; Shuli Jiang; Linsey Pang; Xiongye Xiao; Xiyang Hu
central_claim: Evaluates 72 auditors incl. 11 LLM judges across three information states; argues auditor benchmark numbers are uninterpretable without published label creation.
cite_claim: Monitor/auditor benchmark numbers depend on how labels are produced; label provenance must be published.
quote: The three sharpest results cut against our own data.
relevance: Methodological caution for our detection metrics; label provenance of seeded drifts.

title: Agent Safety Should Be a Runtime Contract
authors: Albus W. Ng; Yi Han; Jusheng Zhang; Wenhao Wang
central_claim: Position: harnesses should enforce preventive checks and evidential checks (proof good actions happened) before a task is accepted.
cite_claim: Position papers call for evidential runtime checks that good actions actually happened.
quote: The evidential face requires verifiable proof that good actions actually happened
relevance: Supports read-after-write/evidential framing.

title: Who Holds the Pen? Let Specifications, Not Agents, Sign Off
authors: Haiqing Li; Xin Ma; Yinhao Wu; Wenliang Zhong; Feng Jiang; Thao M. Dang; Xiao Hu; Hehuan Ma; Yuzhi Guo; Junzhou Huang
central_claim: On SkillsBench, agents' completion claims outpace official pass rates by ~29-38 points; SpecHarness checks verifiable obligations at runtime.
cite_claim: Specifications typically remain context for the same model that acts and declares completion; independent runtime checks are needed.
quote: typically remain context for the same model that acts and declares completion
relevance: Supports independent (non-agent) verification of outcomes.

title: A brief account of runtime verification
authors: Martin Leucker; Christian Schallhart
venue_or_publisher: Journal of Logic and Algebraic Programming 78(5):293-303
central_claim: Foundational overview of runtime verification.
cite_claim: Runtime verification as a field (classical definition) [verify: full text not opened].
quote: [verify] full text not opened; existence confirmed via Luebeck ISP and N. Markey bibliography records
relevance: Classical RV citation for related work.

title: Introduction to Runtime Verification
authors: Ezio Bartocci; Ylies Falcone; Adrian Francalanza; Giles Reger
venue_or_publisher: Lectures on Runtime Verification, LNCS 10457, pp. 1-33, Springer
central_claim: Primer on RV: specification languages, monitoring terminology, instrumentation, monitorability.
cite_claim: Standard RV terminology for monitors, instrumentation and monitorability.
quote: The aim of this chapter is to act as a primer for those wanting to learn about Runtime Verification (RV).
relevance: Classical RV citation for terminology.

title: Building bug-free O-O software: An Introduction to Design by Contract
authors: Eiffel Software (Bertrand Meyer lineage; Meyer, 'Applying Design by Contract', IEEE Computer 25(10), 1992)
central_claim: Contracts assign preconditions to clients and postconditions to suppliers; assertion monitoring checks behavior against intent.
cite_claim: In Design by Contract the supplier (here: the tool) owns the postcondition, so a postcondition violation points at the tool, which motivates fixing the tool rather than the caller.
location: Sec. 3 'The notion of contract'; Sec. 7 'Testing, debugging, quality assurance'
quote: Assertion monitoring is a way to check what the software does against what its author thinks it does.
relevance: DbC lineage; Meyer 1992 PDF is a scan, cite via this page or the IEEE record [verify page numbers].

title: The Daikon system for dynamic detection of likely invariants
authors: Michael D. Ernst; Jeff H. Perkins; Philip J. Guo; Stephen McCamant; Carlos Pacheco; Matthew S. Tschantz; Chen Xiao
central_claim: Reports likely program invariants observed over executions (constants, ranges, linear relations, orderings).
cite_claim: Likely invariants can be inferred from observed executions; classical ancestor of mining outcome contracts from traffic.
quote: Daikon is an implementation of dynamic detection of likely invariants
relevance: Contract-inference baseline (H-RM2).
